definitions.gloss: looks interesting; looks like fun; sounds fun
definitions.explanation: An appearance-based judgement that something seems interesting or enjoyable, based on what the speaker has seen or heard about it. Formed from {面白|おもしろ}い + the evidential suffix そう.

examples.japanese: ⟦その→その：00993_sono⟧⟦{映画|えいが}→映画：02273_eiga⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧{面白|おもしろ}そうだ。
{面白|おもしろ}そうな{本|ほん}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{見|み}つけた→見つける：01180_mitsukeru⟧。

⟦{新|あたら}しい→新しい：00506_atarashii⟧⟦{仕事|しごと}→仕事：00480_shigoto⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{内容|ないよう}→内容：01482_naiyou⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{聞|き}いて→聞く：00483_kiku⟧、⟦とても→とても：00593_totemo⟧{面白|おもしろ}そうだ⟦と→と：00512_to⟧⟦{思|おも}った→思う：00492_omou⟧。
examples.english: After hearing what the new job involves, I thought it sounded really interesting.

notes:
Formed by attaching the evidential そう suffix to the stem of the i-adjective ⟦{面白|おもしろ}い→面白い：00589_omoshiroi⟧ (drop い, add そう). The result conjugates as a na-adjective: {面白|おもしろ}そうだ (predicate) / {面白|おもしろ}そうな (modifier) / {面白|おもしろ}そう⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧ (adverbial).

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {面白|おもしろ}そうな⟦{話|はなし}→話：01496_hanashi⟧: an interesting-sounding story
- {面白|おもしろ}そう⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{聞|き}こえる→聞こえる：01229_kikoeru⟧: to sound interesting
- {面白|おもしろ}そうにして⟦いる→いる：00495_iru⟧: to look like one is having fun

USAGE:
Used only when the speaker has not yet experienced the thing directly. After actually trying it, switch to plain ⟦{面白|おもしろ}い→面白い：00589_omoshiroi⟧. Saying *{面白|おもしろ}そうな⟦{映画|えいが}→映画：02273_eiga⟧だった about a movie you have already watched sounds odd.
